$comment: Render v2 registry: the ONE source for the view library. Edit here, then run python3 tools/gen_views.py (writes views/library.json, views/prompt/*.md, views/checkers.json and the SCHEMA.md views block). Plan: brain projects/calc/topics/openui-render-arch-plan-2026-10-18.md (START HERE v2, Appendix v1 §16); caps and locks: refine/REFINE.md F2 F3 F4 F5 F7 F11 F19, VISUAL-FIRST. Prop shapes = the P1.1 renderer's (views-lib.js reads them from library.json). props: ordered (positional order), JSON Schema each; {"x-any": true} = any shipped component. ships: P1.1 = drawn by views.js, emitted into library.json; planned = roadmap only (table in SCHEMA.md, never in a prompt).

layers.L0: primitives (escape hatch): build anything when no learning component fits
layers.L1: learning components: subject-blind, know data shapes only
layers.L2: renderers of engine data: every value comes from an engine result

wrong.desc: the picked distractor: wrong.error tag, wrong.text

key.desc: hidden answer values (key.v1); the gate drops any key ref, or literal equal to a key value, outside post

gate.desc: statement parses as OpenUI Lang (profile stem: no Mutation, no Action, no timers)
component exists in this library; args match its props, caps included (over a cap: drop, log too-long)
Query tool exists in the engine list; runs SERVER side; the browser gets results only
domain component: its checker re-runs the engine and compares
no key ref and no literal equal to a hidden value outside post; a Reveal body is a second program
recipe allows this stage; refs allowed in this stage
every state word in nodes / edges / marks / Legend items is one of marks
at most one Steps or Compare per root; one figure per Steps
no string holds a hex colour, px, an emoji, or an all-caps word over 3 letters that is no code

copy_gate.py on the view's student-facing strings: Flesch-Kincaid grade 2-4 on the whole view text (TeX and numbers stripped; skipped under 20 words), no term from views/allow/<course>-black.json (tools/jargon.py), no slot over its character budget, no blocking aiw.lint_view_strings finding
a Steps whose fig is a Scene: scene components only inside it (Q in qs, Ask on a Step); geom keys per kind; scene Steps leave the Graph args null; Q roles (an answer has an expr and never a value)

ids match ^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]{0,15}$, are unique in the scene (objects, Axes items, Q), are not reserved; every op / relation / anchor / {token} / q / code id exists; every object is added by some step
relations parse (attach on pivot align distribute stack set scale), form a directed acyclic graph, one writer per prop
every expression parses with the one EBNF (views/scene-contract.md §3) and evaluates finite, |v| <= 10000
the server runs each Trace's Code (Python subset) and writes its ticks; the model never writes them
ops parse (add set glow hide camera param), set only settable props, act on visible ids
3-6 steps; one change per step after the first; the last step shows geometry; an ask before the last, answered by the next step; density 12 marks / 6 labels; captions <= 15 words

before a solve (stage pre / wrong, set by the server) no string number and no given / derived value hits the answer (3 sig figs or 0.5%, unit variants); string numbers are givens; middle values allowed
captions talk to the student and pass the voice lints (no dashes, no !, no hype, no not-X-but-Y, no question answered, no objects acting like people)
a failing scene: one repair round with the error list (max 10), then the Steps is dropped and the reply goes out text only

slot.desc: Slot convention (views plan Oct 20): any student-facing string may be the whole literal "$t.<id>"; views.js fills it from the view's t map (render option t: {id: text}), and an id with no text paints as an outlined empty box (data-slot=<id>) for measure_slots. Caps apply to the filled text, not the ref. components.<C>.words names every prop that carries student-facing text, with its UI role (shadcn naming) and expected word class; not_words lists the string props that carry data (marks, ids, TeX, coordinates), never words.

View.desc: The root: its children are painted in order, each into a slot reserved when the root arrives

Head.desc: Title and one-line subtitle of a view

Text.desc: A paragraph; **bold** is the only emphasis

Legend.desc: Legend chips, each "mark label"; the sample is drawn with the figure's own class

Table.desc: A small table: header cells, then rows of cells

Math.desc: Display TeX; an identity it states is re-checked

Chips.desc: A row of small chips (givens, tags)

Callout.desc: A section with a rule and a short tag ("Where it breaks"), never a box

Steps.desc: A stepper: one figure, the steps, an optional frontier row and status table; Back/Next below

Step.desc: One step: caption, node marks "A:cur B:front", edge marks "A-B:tree", tags "A:0", edge labels ["A-B:new"], frontier, table rows

Hints.desc: A hint ladder: one hint at a time

Predict.desc: Pick an answer; the pick is posted with the answer ref to the server, the page never resolves or draws it

Reveal.desc: A visible locked row; its body arrives as a second program when the stage changes

Answer.desc: The boxed answer and one sentence

Doodle.desc: A small drawing when nothing else fits (visual first)

Compare.desc: Two side by side, stepped together

Assume.desc: "I read this as X" chip; a tap sends a refine request

Graph.desc: A graph: nodes "A 48 100, B 160 48", edges "A>B, A-C" (> directed), column labels "48 depth 0", marks "A:done u0:k1"

Geometry.desc: A to-scale geometry figure: named points "A 0,0; B 3,0; C 3,4" (y up), marks seg(A,B) circle(O,2) right(B,A,C) dim(A,B,3 m) angle(A,B,C,$\theta$) arrow(A,C,$F$) label(C,top); at most 12 points, 12 marks, 6 labels; a number in a label is a given, never the answer

label_words.desc: the text argument of dim / angle / arrow / label: student-facing, may be a whole "$t.<id>" slot

Scene.desc: A scene in world units (y up): objects, quantities, relations; only as Steps.fig. The renderer solves it and owns every pixel and label spot (views/scene-contract.md)

Shape.desc: A shape: geom "w=10 h=0.4 segments=10", at a point "0,3" or an anchor "rod.right"; label may hold {qid} tokens

Link.desc: A connector between two points or anchors; a vector's to may be relative "+0,-1.5"; q = a Q id

Axes.desc: A plot frame: x / y "min,max label", items "f curve x^2/2+1", "R riemann f 0 4 n left", "m marker y 60 your guess"

MathRows.desc: Math, one step per row, aligned on the first =; {qid} tokens

Code.desc: Source lines; the highlight follows a Trace or set hl

Trace.desc: The engine runs a Code and shows vars per tick; never write ticks (the server fills them)

Cells.desc: An array, stack or grid of cells; ptrs "i:0 j:4"

Bars.desc: Bars "label: expr"; conserve = they share the total, so a drain shows

Q.desc: A quantity: given (value), derived (expr), answer (expr, shown only after a solve), unknown (symbol)

Ask.desc: A question with 2-4 choices on a scene step; the next step shows the answer to it

FlowNet.desc: Flow network with flows and the min cut

FBD.desc: Free-body diagram; magnitudes from the engine

Timeline.desc: Ordered events on a line (history or motion)

misconception.desc: where the picked idea breaks, first; then the fix

predict-reveal.desc: ask a pick, the server marks it, the Reveal body arrives as a patch

steps.desc: worked steps, one at a time

twin-compare.desc: two methods or two algorithms side by side, in sync

slider-explore.desc: drag a parameter, watch the verdict change

scene-steps.desc: a step-through scene: objects in world units, one change per tap, an ask before the end (views/scene-contract.md)
rules: Goals, in order: the student understands, stays engaged, the figure is true.
Write one `Steps(<Scene>, [steps])`. Declare every object once in the Scene with an id; steps only name ids.
Never write a pixel, a colour or a size word. World units, y up, degrees counter-clockwise. The site places every label.
Numbers you write: givens from the problem, small counts, or a Q expr. Never the answer: give it a Q with role answer and an expr (no value); the site shows its symbol until the student solves it.
A middle value is a derived Q with an expr; write `{qid}` in a caption, label or row to show it.
Shape geom: rect `w= h=` [`radius= segments= rotate=`]; circle `r=`; triangle `base= height=` [`apex=`]; polygon `pts=x,y;x,y;x,y`; line `from= to=`; point `""`.
Anchors: `rod.right`, `rod.top@0.3` (along an edge), `ceil@0.2` (along a line or Link), `ramp.hyp@0.5`; a bare id is its center. Anchors follow the object every step.
Link kinds: arrow, vector (`to` may be `+dx,dy`), spring `coils=`, string, dimension `offset=`, angle `at= r=`. `q` names the Q that sets a vector's length.
Axes items: `f curve <expr in x>`, `p line x,y;x,y`, `A area f a b`, `R riemann f a b n left|right|mid|trap`, `t tangent f x0`, `d pointon f x`, `m marker x|y v label`.
Relations (rels): `attach sp.end ball.left`, `on ball ramp.hyp 0.3`, `pivot rod rod.right`, `align a b bottom`, `distribute a b c x`, `stack cu al x`, `set al.w 2*cu.w`, `scale Fg Fn`. No cycles.
Expressions: numbers, Q ids, `id.prop` (w h r base height apex radius segments rotate x y len), `+ - * / ^ ( )`, sqrt sin cos tan abs min max rad pi. No 1e3, no 2x.
A scene step: `Step("caption", null, null, null, null, null, null, [ops], Ask("q", [choices]))`; the six nulls skip the graph args; Ask is optional.
Ops (at most 4, 40 chars each): `add a b`, `set rod rotate -6`, `glow a b` (this step only), `hide a`, `camera fit a b` or `camera all`, `param n 8`.
Step 1 sets the scene (what the student already has). After it: one change per step (one id added, set, hidden or param'd); glow and camera are free.
3 to 6 steps. The last step adds or moves geometry, not only math. Ask once before the last step; the next step shows the answer to it.
Captions: at most 15 words, talk to the student (you, a command, or a question). No dashes, no !, no let's, no hype, no objects acting like people. A dense last step: split it in two.
Trace: write the Code and `Trace(id, codeId, "i total")`; the server runs it and fills the ticks; step with `set tr tick k`.
Bars with conserve: the items sum to the total in every step; drain one with param or set.

mechanics: Bodies are rect / circle / triangle Shapes; forces are vector Links from an anchor on the body; forces you compare share one `scale`.
Torque: a point at the pivot, dimension Links for the lever arms with `{arm}` labels; tilt with `set rod rotate -6`, level with `set rod rotate 0`.
Ramps: a triangle with apex 0; put a body on it with `on ball ramp.hyp 0.3`; energy as Bars with conserve.
Strings and springs end on anchors, so they follow a moving body.
Heat or flow through joined rods: `stack cu al x`, `set al.w 2*cu.w`, the profile as an Axes line, the student's guess as a marker.
calc: One Axes per scene; short curve ids (f, g); ranges from the givens.
Riemann: `R riemann f a b n left` with n a given Q; double it with `param n 8`; the exact area is the answer Q.
Tangent or secant: `t tangent f x0`, move it with `set t x 1.5`.
The student's guess: `m marker y v your guess` (their number is a given).
cs_trace: Code lines exactly as the problem has them; one Trace bound to the Code; `set tr tick k` moves one tick per step.
Cells for the list being walked; move a pointer with `set ar ptr.i 3`.
Never write a loop value yourself: the trace computes it, and the final value stays hidden until the solve.

example: st = Steps(sc, [p1, p2, p3, p4, p5, p6])
sc = Scene([ceil, rod, s1t, s2t, Wv, pv, dT, dW, eq], [T1, L, armT1, armW, W], ["pivot rod rod.right"], "A rod hung from two strings, with its weight at the middle.")
ceil = Shape("ceil", "line", "from=0,6 to=10,6", null, null, null, "ground")
p1 = Step("You took torques about the right end. Where does T1 pull?", null, null, null, null, null, null, ["add ceil rod s1t s2t Wv pv", "glow pv s1t"])
p2 = Step("Count the segments from T1 to your pivot.", null, null, null, null, null, null, ["add dT", "glow dT"])
p3 = Step("Now count from the weight to the pivot.", null, null, null, null, null, null, ["add dW", "glow dW"], Ask("Which pull has the longer arm?", ["T1", "W"]))
p4 = Step("Watch the rod tilt toward the longer arm.", null, null, null, null, null, null, ["set rod rotate -6", "glow dT"])
p5 = Step("Write both turns as one equation.", null, null, null, null, null, null, ["add eq", "glow eq"])
p6 = Step("Level the rod and solve that line for W yourself.", null, null, null, null, null, null, ["set rod rotate 0", "glow eq Wv"])

answer-table.desc: the answer + the table that proves it (post only)
